corpus.description: 20 born-digital academic PDFs, mostly two-column journal articles
corpus.note: the PDFs themselves are copyrighted and are NOT in this repo; only metrics are

harness.ranking_signal: median per-page OCR recall vs the rendered page (visual.py)

caveat: visual_order is measured against tesseract's own reading order, which is unreliable on complex layouts. It is trustworthy for GROSS differences and not for fine ranking. The pdftotext-vs-docling order gap below is gross (0.52-0.70 vs 0.96-1.00) and consistent in direction across 10 of 17 documents, which is why it is reported as a result; both backends are scored against the SAME reference per page, so a scrambled reference would penalise both.

verdict.docling_rationale: reading order on two-column papers: median 1.000 vs pdftotext 0.697, clearly better on 10/17 and worse on 1/17. Recall is a tie (0.931 vs 0.945), so the slot is earned on ORDER, which is what tier 3 is for. Two documents where pdftotext scored 0.000 recall and docling 0.978/0.945 are the escalation case working.
verdict.marker_rationale: failed 16 of 20 documents on this deployment (vllm inference server would not start), so there is no paired basis to rank it. On the 4 it completed it is indistinguishable from docling. The failure is deployment-specific rather than intrinsic to marker, but the ladder must work on the machine it runs on, so that does not rescue it. marker stays selectable via --tier marker and out of `auto`.
